reference.title: Bent knee Lying Twist (male)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips; Waist, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Inhale as the knees lower to the side, exhale as you pull them back to the middle.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s down, short pause, about 1.5 s back

prescription.tempo: About 1.5 s to the side, brief pause, 1.5 s back
prescription.progression: Larger range, slower tempo, then straight legs (windshield wipers)

cues.text: Lie on your back, arms out to the sides palms down. Lift the legs so the hips and knees are bent about 90 degrees, knees together.
Breathe in and lower both knees slowly to the right; the left shoulder stays heavy on the mat.
Pause, breathe out and pull the knees back over the hips with the obliques.
Lower to the left only as far as both shoulders stay down.
Breathe out and return to the middle without swinging.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the legs drop and bounce off the floor
mistakes.fix: Lower in about 1.5 s and stop before you lose control.

mistakes.mistake: The opposite shoulder lifting off the mat
mistakes.fix: Shorten the range; press both arms into the floor.

mistakes.mistake: Low back arching as the legs travel
mistakes.fix: Brace gently and keep the ribs down.

kinematics.norm: As far as the shoulders stay down; no study defines the range (clinical opinion)
Shared by the lumbar and thoracic spine while the upper back stays on the mat; the lumbar segments rotate only a little (clinical opinion)
Arms out in a T, shoulders down (clinical opinion)
Slow and controlled, about 1.5 s each way (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #363912, Bent knee Lying Twist (male), video (movement reference)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Low-back pain: keep the range small and the knees bent, or keep the feet on the floor; stop if twisting provokes pain (clinical opinion).
Osteoporosis or vertebral fracture: avoid repeated loaded spinal flexion and twisting.
Pregnancy and postpartum (diastasis recti): get individual guidance before dynamic trunk-flexion work.
The athlete mesh rests on the mat; the rig collision shapes are thicker than the mesh at the back and buttocks, so floorTolerance records how far those proxy shapes sink below the mat surface.
modify: Feet on the floor (knee rocks) to make it easier.
Smaller range: knees only part of the way to the floor.
regressions: Supine knee rocks with the feet on the floor.
progressions: Slower lowering with a 2 s pause near the floor.
Light medicine ball between the knees.

muscleNotes.obliques_r: External and internal obliques lower the legs to the side under control and pull them back to the middle; they are the trunk rotators (the twisting cross curl-up raised external oblique activity over a straight curl-up, Konrad 2001). No study measured this exact drill (clinical opinion for the rest).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: External and internal obliques lower the legs to the side under control and pull them back to the middle; they are the trunk rotators (the twisting cross curl-up raised external oblique activity over a straight curl-up, Konrad 2001). No study measured this exact drill (clinical opinion for the rest).
muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis and the deep abdominals hold the pelvis so the low back does not arch as the legs travel (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Hold the thighs up at about 90 degrees (tabletop) throughout (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Hold the thighs up at about 90 degrees (tabletop) throughout (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Keep the knees and feet together (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Keep the knees and feet together (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Press the arms into the mat to keep the shoulders down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Press the arms into the mat to keep the shoulders down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Helps press the outstretched arms into the floor for an anchor (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Helps press the outstretched arms into the floor for an anchor (clinical opinion).
